title: Binary search on the answer
objective: Binary search over possible answers when a "does this work?" check only gets easier as the answer grows.

sources.title: Laaksonen, Competitive Programmer's Handbook: binary search: finding the smallest solution

simplifies: Each check here runs need() over every parcel, which is fine for small inputs. The key condition is monotonic: if capacity c works, every bigger capacity works too.

quiz.prompt: Why does binary search work on the capacity?

options.text: If a capacity works, every bigger capacity works too, so the answers line up like a sorted list
options.explanation: Right. That one-way switch, from "no" to "yes", is all binary search needs.

options.text: Because the parcel weights are sorted
options.explanation: They don't need to be; it is the yes/no answers over capacities that are ordered.
Whole numbers help us stop, but the ordering of yes/no answers is the real reason.

options.text: A truck smaller than the heaviest parcel can never carry it
options.explanation: Right. Anything below that can be ruled out without checking.
It might be, but often a bigger capacity is needed to fit the day limit.

options.text: To make the loop shorter only
options.explanation: It does shorten the search, but the reason is that smaller values are impossible.
